claim: Nemaline myopathy (NM) affects approximately 1 in 50,000 births.
source: Nemaline myopathy (NM) is one of the most severe forms of congenital myopathy, affecting ~1 in 50,000 births (Romero et al., 2013; Wallgren-Pettersson et al., 2011).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research (Romero et al., 2013; Wallgren-Pettersson et al., 2011).

claim: Nemaline myopathy is one of the most severe forms of congenital myopathy.

claim: Nemaline bodies are formed by the abnormal aggregation of proteins within muscle thin filaments.
source: Nemaline bodies are formed by the abnormal aggregation of proteins within muscle thin filaments and are associated with myofibril disorganization, reduced contractile force, mitochondrial dysfunction, and a spectrum of abnormalities ranging from mild muscle weakness to complete akinesia.
evidence: This is a statement of established scientific knowledge about nemaline bodies.

claim: Mutations in 11 different genes have been linked to nemaline myopathy.
source: To date, mutations in 11 different genes have been linked to NM, most of which encode components of the sarcomeric thin filament, including nebulin (NEB), actin-1, tropomyosins-2 and -3, troponin-1 and leiomodin-3 (LMOD3) (Agrawal et al., 2004; Cenik et al., 2015; Donner et al., 2002; Johnston et al., 2000; Lehtokari et al., 2006; Wattanasirichaigoon et al., 2002; Yuen et al., 2014).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to published research.

claim: Most genes linked to nemaline myopathy encode components of the sarcomeric thin filament.

claim: Three genes associated with nemaline myopathy (KLHL40, KLHL41 and KBTBD13) encode Kelch proteins.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research (Geyer et al., 2003; Gupta and Beggs, 2014).

source: However, there are also Kelch proteins that function independently of proteolysis (Werner et al., 2015) and much remains to be learned about their functions.

claim: Loss of function of KLHL40 in mice causes nemaline myopathy similar to that seen in human patients with KLHL40 mutations.
source: Recently, we and others showed that loss of function of the muscle-specific Kelch protein KLHL40 in mice causes NM similar to that seen in human patients with KLHL40 mutations (Garg et al., 2014; Ravenscroft et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research (Garg et al., 2014; Ravenscroft et al., 2013).

claim: KLHL40 is required for stabilization of LMOD3.

evidence: The claim is supported by citations to published research (Cenik et al., 2015; Garg et al., 2014).

source: The absence of LMOD3 or NEB causes lethal NM and severe disruption of skeletal muscle sarcomeric structure and function in mice and humans, confirming the essential roles of these proteins in maintenance of sarcomere integrity.
evidence: This is a statement based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: KLHL41 mutations in humans have been associated with nemaline myopathy.

claim: Klhl41 is expressed with highest levels in adult skeletal muscle relative to the heart.
source: Klhl41 is expressed in a muscle-specific manner with highest levels in adult skeletal muscle relative to the heart (Figure 1A–B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1A-B.

claim: Klhl41 is highly expressed in somite myotomes at embryonic day (E) 10.5.
source: During embryogenesis, Klhl41 is highly expressed in somite myotomes at embryonic day (E) 10.5 and in skeletal muscles throughout the body at later stages, as detected by in situ hybridization (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Klhl41 is expressed in skeletal muscles throughout the body at later embryonic stages.
source: During embryogenesis, Klhl41 is highly expressed in somite myotomes at embryonic day (E) 10.5 and in skeletal muscles throughout the body at later stages, as detected by in situ hybridization (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Mice heterozygous for the Klhl41 mutant allele (Klhl41+/−) were normal.
source: Mice heterozygous for the mutant allele (Klhl41+/−) were normal and were intercrossed to obtain Klhl41−/−knockout (KO) mice.
evidence: This is a statement based on experimental observations.

claim: LacZ expression was not detected in Klhl41+/− mice.
source: LacZ expression was not detected in Klhl41+/− mice, suggesting that the LacZ cassette was spliced out.
evidence: This is a statement based on experimental observations.

claim: The LacZ cassette was spliced out in Klhl41+/− mice.
source: LacZ expression was not detected in Klhl41+/− mice, suggesting that the LacZ cassette was spliced out.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that LacZ expression was not detected.

claim: Quantitative RT-PCR confirmed the complete loss of Klhl41 transcript in KO mice.
source: Quantitative RT-PCR (qRT-PCR) confirmed the complete loss of Klhl41 transcript in KO mice (Figure 2A) and western blot analysis revealed loss of KLHL41 protein in muscle from KO mice (Figure 2B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Western blot analysis revealed loss of KLHL41 protein in muscle from KO mice.

claim: Klhl41 KO mice were born at Mendelian ratios from heterozygous intercrosses.
source: KO mice were born at Mendelian ratios from heterozygous intercrosses and were indistinguishable from WT littermates at birth (Figure 2C).

claim: Klhl41 KO mice were indistinguishable from WT littermates at birth.
source: KO mice were born at Mendelian ratios from heterozygous intercrosses and were indistinguishable from WT littermates at birth (Figure 2C).

claim: Klhl41 KO pups failed to thrive.
source: However, KO pups failed to thrive and showed progressive lethality from birth to postnatal day (P) 12, after which no surviving KO mice were observed (Figure 2D).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Klhl41 KO pups showed progressive lethality from birth to postnatal day (P) 12.

claim: No surviving Klhl41 KO mice were observed after postnatal day (P) 12.

claim: Klhl41 KO mice had milk spots comparable to those of their WT littermates.
source: In order to ascertain that the failure to thrive was not due to difficulty in suckling or breathing, we confirmed that KO mice had milk spots comparable to those of their WT littermates.
evidence: This is a statement based on experimental observations.

claim: Klhl41 KO mice that survived the early neonatal period displayed severe runting at P3 and P10.
source: KO mice that survived the early neonatal period displayed severe runting at P3 and P10 (Figure 2C), and their body weight failed to increase with age (Figure 2E), even when other littermates were removed from their mothers, indicating an intrinsic abnormality rather than simply an inability to compete with stronger siblings for nursing.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The body weight of Klhl41 KO mice failed to increase with age.

evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2E.

claim: The failure to thrive in Klhl41 KO mice indicates an intrinsic abnormality rather than simply an inability to compete with stronger siblings for nursing.
source: KO mice that survived the early neonatal period displayed severe runting at P3 and P10 (Figure 2C), and their body weight failed to increase with age (Figure 2E), even when other littermates were removed from their mothers, indicating an intrinsic abnormality rather than simply an inability to compete with stronger siblings for nursing.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that body weight failed to increase even when other littermates were removed.

claim: Occasional ragged fibers were observed in the diaphragm of Klhl41 KO mice at P0 and P10.
source: Histological analysis of skeletal muscles of KO mice at various time points revealed occasional ragged fibers (fibers with discontinuities in their staining) in the diaphragm and the hindlimbs at P0 and P10 (Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Occasional ragged fibers were observed in the hindlimbs of Klhl41 KO mice at P0 and P10.

evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Klhl41 KO myofibers presented abundant depositions that were absent in WT muscle.
source: Further abnormalities in muscle histology were observed by Gomori's trichrome staining (Figure 3B). KO myofibers presented abundant depositions that were absent in WT muscle.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Desmin protein aggregates were distributed across myofibers in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Desmin staining showed additional cytoskeletal disarray (Figure 3C). In WT muscle at P3, desmin was evenly expressed throughout transverse sections of myofibers. However, in KO mice, desmin protein aggregates were distributed across myofibers, indicating abnormal sarcomere structure (Figure 3C).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Desmin protein aggregates in Klhl41 KO mice indicate abnormal sarcomere structure.
source: Desmin staining showed additional cytoskeletal disarray (Figure 3C). In WT muscle at P3, desmin was evenly expressed throughout transverse sections of myofibers. However, in KO mice, desmin protein aggregates were distributed across myofibers, indicating abnormal sarcomere structure (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of desmin protein aggregates.

claim: A similar general disarray in sarcomeric α-actinin staining was observed in Klhl41 KO muscle.
source: We observed a similar general disarray in sarcomeric α-actinin staining in KO muscle (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Electron microscopy of diaphragm at P3 showed sarcomere disarray in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Electron microscopy of diaphragm (Figure 3D–E) and hindlimb muscle (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) at P3 also showed sarcomere disarray and Z-line streaming, as well as electron dense inclusions, corresponding to nemaline bodies.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3D-E.

claim: Electron microscopy of diaphragm at P3 showed Z-line streaming in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Electron microscopy of diaphragm (Figure 3D–E) and hindlimb muscle (Figure 3—figure supplement 2) at P3 also showed sarcomere disarray and Z-line streaming, as well as electron dense inclusions, corresponding to nemaline bodies.

claim: Hearts from WT and Klhl41 KO mice were indistinguishable.
source: Hearts from WT and KO mice were indistinguishable (Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Quantitative proteomics revealed a total of 389 proteins that were up- or down-regulated in muscle from Klhl41 KO mice.
source: To further define the muscle abnormalities of Klhl41 KO mice, we compared the protein compositions of WT and Klhl41 KO hindlimb muscle at P0 by unbiased quantitative proteomics. These studies revealed a total of 389 proteins that were up- or down-regulated in muscle from the KO mice, with KLHL41 being the most down-regulated protein (Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: KLHL41 was the most down-regulated protein in muscle from Klhl41 KO mice.
source: To further define the muscle abnormalities of Klhl41 KO mice, we compared the protein compositions of WT and Klhl41 KO hindlimb muscle at P0 by unbiased quantitative proteomics. These studies revealed a total of 389 proteins that were up- or down-regulated in muscle from the KO mice, with KLHL41 being the most down-regulated protein (Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 1.

claim: 'Sarcomere organization' proteins were aberrantly down-regulated in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Analysis of enriched biological pathways using the Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID) (Jiao et al., 2012) revealed that 'sarcomere organization' and 'regulation of muscle contraction' proteins were aberrantly down-regulated in KO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: 'Regulation of muscle contraction' proteins were aberrantly down-regulated in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Analysis of enriched biological pathways using the Database for Annotation, Visualization and Integrated Discovery (DAVID) (Jiao et al., 2012) revealed that 'sarcomere organization' and 'regulation of muscle contraction' proteins were aberrantly down-regulated in KO mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: NEB was the second most down-regulated protein in the muscle of Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Remarkably, NEB was the second most down-regulated protein in the muscle of the KO mice (Figure 4A).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Many down-regulated proteins in Klhl41 KO mice were essential components of the sarcomere.
source: Many other down-regulated proteins in the KO mice were essential components of the sarcomere (Figure 4B), including slow skeletal muscle troponin T, myosin light chain-3, myozenin-3, and β-tropomyosin (also associated with NM).
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: The mRNAs encoding down-regulated proteins in Klhl41 KO mice were unchanged.
source: As revealed by deep sequencing of RNA transcripts (Figure 4—source data 2), the mRNAs encoding these proteins were unchanged in KO muscle. Therefore, the changes in accumulation of these proteins likely reflect post-translational mechanisms.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4—source data 2.

claim: The changes in accumulation of proteins in Klhl41 KO mice likely reflect post-translational mechanisms.
source: As revealed by deep sequencing of RNA transcripts (Figure 4—source data 2), the mRNAs encoding these proteins were unchanged in KO muscle. Therefore, the changes in accumulation of these proteins likely reflect post-translational mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that mRNA levels were unchanged.

claim: Western blot analysis showed down-regulation of NEB in Klhl41 KO mice.

evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Western blot analysis showed only a slight decrease in LMOD3 in Klhl41 KO mice.

evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Both NEB and LMOD3 were markedly down-regulated in Klhl40 KO mice.

claim: The mRNA levels of NEB and LMOD3 did not change in Klhl41 KO muscle.

claim: KLHL41 could mainly stabilize NEB instead of LMOD3.
source: We therefore reasoned that KLHL41 could mainly stabilize NEB instead of LMOD3, further underscoring the possibility that these two Kelch proteins act, at least partially, through different mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NEB was more down-regulated than LMOD3 in Klhl41 KO mice.

claim: KLHL40 and KLHL41 act, at least partially, through different mechanisms.
source: We therefore reasoned that KLHL41 could mainly stabilize NEB instead of LMOD3, further underscoring the possibility that these two Kelch proteins act, at least partially, through different mechanisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that KLHL41 and KLHL40 have different effects on NEB and LMOD3.

claim: Nebulin-related anchoring protein (NRAP) was up-regulated at protein levels in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Nebulin-related anchoring protein (NRAP), another member of the nebulin family (Pappas et al., 2011), was up-regulated both at protein and mRNA levels (probably as a compensatory consequence of sarcomere disarray) (Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 2), suggesting that the presence of nebulin repeats is not sufficient for KLHL41 to recognize and stabilize its partners.
evidence: The claim is supported by data shown in Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 2.

claim: Nebulin-related anchoring protein (NRAP) was up-regulated at mRNA levels in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: Nebulin-related anchoring protein (NRAP), another member of the nebulin family (Pappas et al., 2011), was up-regulated both at protein and mRNA levels (probably as a compensatory consequence of sarcomere disarray) (Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 2), suggesting that the presence of nebulin repeats is not sufficient for KLHL41 to recognize and stabilize its partners.

claim: The up-regulation of NRAP in Klhl41 KO mice is probably a compensatory consequence of sarcomere disarray.
source: Nebulin-related anchoring protein (NRAP), another member of the nebulin family (Pappas et al., 2011), was up-regulated both at protein and mRNA levels (probably as a compensatory consequence of sarcomere disarray) (Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 2), suggesting that the presence of nebulin repeats is not sufficient for KLHL41 to recognize and stabilize its partners.
evidence: This is speculation about the reason for NRAP up-regulation.

claim: The presence of nebulin repeats is not sufficient for KLHL41 to recognize and stabilize its partners.
source: Nebulin-related anchoring protein (NRAP), another member of the nebulin family (Pappas et al., 2011), was up-regulated both at protein and mRNA levels (probably as a compensatory consequence of sarcomere disarray) (Figure 4A and Figure 4—source data 2), suggesting that the presence of nebulin repeats is not sufficient for KLHL41 to recognize and stabilize its partners.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that NRAP was up-regulated despite having nebulin repeats.

claim: LMOD2 was up-regulated at protein levels in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: In contrast to LMOD3, LMOD2, another member of the LMOD family involved in thin filament shortening and cardiomyopathy (Pappas et al., 2015), was also up-regulated in Klhl41 KO mice both at protein and mRNA levels.
evidence: This is a statement based on experimental observations.

claim: LMOD2 was up-regulated at mRNA levels in Klhl41 KO mice.
source: In contrast to LMOD3, LMOD2, another member of the LMOD family involved in thin filament shortening and cardiomyopathy (Pappas et al., 2015), was also up-regulated in Klhl41 KO mice both at protein and mRNA levels.
